title: Exceptional Kunneth; the $\alpha$ map
statement:
For $i=1,2$, let $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ be morphisms of separated
finite-type schemes satisfying the
exceptional-adjoint admissibility of
[def-trf-admissibility], and let $L_i\in D^b_{ctf}(Y_i,A)$. The
canonical comparison of [def-sf-kv-maps] (ii), formed with the geometric operations,

$$
\alpha:f_1^!L_1\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L} f_2^!L_2
\longrightarrow
(f_1\times f_2)^!\bigl(L_1\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L} L_2\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism, natural in the $L_i$.

proof.text:
Work at the finite stage $A=A_{E,n}$ and with the specified constructible adjunctions $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$ of [def-trf-admissibility], on $D^b_{ctf}$ over $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$. Preservation is [thm-sf-ctf-stability]; [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] supplies the etale-origin witnesses required by [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale].

Put $B=Y_1\times Y_2$, $P=X_1\times Y_2$, $Q=Y_1\times X_2$, with product maps $a:P\to B$, $b:Q\to B$ and projections $r:P\times_BQ\to P$, $s:P\times_BQ\to Q$. For $M=p_{X_1}^*B_1$, $N=p_{X_2}^*B_2$, apply the existing [thm-sf-kunneth-relative] to $(a,b,M,N)$:
$$R(bs)_!(r^*M\otimes^Ls^*N)\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_!M\otimes^LRb_!N.$$
The geometric projection and composition isomorphisms required there are [fix-prop-projection-formula] and [thm-sf-comp-composition]; base change is the finite witnessed theorem just cited. The two product-square exchanges identify $p_{Y_1}^*Rf_{1!}B_1\cong Ra_!M$ and $p_{Y_2}^*Rf_{2!}B_2\cong Rb_!N$. Compose with their inverses tensored together. This is exactly $\mathrm{Ku}_!$ of [def-sf-kv-maps](i), with $(T,U,V,W,u,v,p,q)=(B,P,Q,P\times_BQ,a,b,r,s)$. Product-square arrows are separated finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. Substituting $B_i=f_i^!L_i$ and composing with $\varepsilon_1\boxtimes\varepsilon_2$ has exceptional transpose precisely $\alpha$ of clause (ii). Only the finite specialization of that definition is used.

source.place: paragraph 1: shriek Kunneth and definition of alpha

proof.text:
We will use the following consequences of the specified adjunctions, keeping track of the arrow $\alpha$. The composition comparison is precisely that specified in [def-trf-admissibility]: all composable maps below are separated of finite type between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, so its constructible adjunction and composition clauses apply on the stated finite-Tor categories. The conjugate of $R(gf)_!\cong Rg_!Rf_!$ gives $c:(gf)^!\cong f^!g^!$, by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]; its counit is $\varepsilon_g\circ Rg_!(\varepsilon_f)g^!$. For pairs of composites $g_if_i$, the product comparison, under this $c$, is
$$
\alpha_{g_1f_1,g_2f_2}(L_1,L_2)
=c^{-1}\circ(f_1\times f_2)^!\bigl(\alpha_{g_1,g_2}(L_1,L_2)\bigr)
 \circ\alpha_{f_1,f_2}(g_1^!L_1,g_2^!L_2).
$$
To check the identity, take its exceptional transpose. The two paths first apply the product comparison for compact support and then apply $\varepsilon_{g_1}\boxtimes\varepsilon_{g_2}$ after $Rg_{1!}\varepsilon_{f_1}\boxtimes Rg_{2!}\varepsilon_{f_2}$. They agree by the projection-formula composition compatibility in [fix-prop-projection-formula], exchange pasting in [fix-lem-exchanges], and the product symmetry, base-change and projection compatibilities in [lem-sf-kunneth-coherence]. This is the pasting identity [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2), with the composite counits just written. Thus the comparisons used below are comparisons of the specified maps, not arbitrary isomorphisms between their endpoints.

source.place: paragraphs 2, 3, 5 and 6: composition and mate-calculus compatibilities

proof.text:
For later use derive dual base change directly on the actual bounded finite-Tor categories. In a cartesian square with vertical maps $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$ and horizontal maps $g:Y'\to Y$, $g':X'\to X$, assume all four arrows are separated of finite type between finite-type $k$-schemes (as holds for the open and closed immersion squares used below). Then the adjunctions of [def-trf-admissibility] and $Lg^*\dashv Rg_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] give, for $H\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and $M\in D^b_{ctf}(Y',A)$,
$$
\operatorname{Hom}(H,f^!Rg_*M)
 \cong\operatorname{Hom}(Lg^*Rf_!H,M)
 \cong\operatorname{Hom}(Rf'_!Lg'^*H,M)
 \cong\operatorname{Hom}(H,Rg'_*f'^!M).
$$
The middle bijection is [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale], applicable by the etale origins in Step 1. These natural Hom bijections define mutually inverse maps by taking the images of the identity maps (the representing-object argument), giving $f^!Rg_*\cong Rg'_*f'^!$. The current statement of [def-trf-admissibility] specifies the opposite-direction exchange $Rg'_*Rf'^!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf^!Rg_*$. The displayed Hom calculation therefore uses its inverse. Equivalently this is the inverse of the conjugate of $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ under the two composite adjunctions, as defined in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. It respects counits and pasted squares by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. No assertion that an arbitrary square mate of an isomorphism is invertible is used: this is conjugation between right adjoints of two isomorphic left adjoints. All the representing objects lie in the stated category by [thm-sf-ctf-stability]. The base-changed vertical morphism has the required separated finite-type property by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change].

source.place: paragraphs 5 and 6: dual base change for closed and open immersions

proof.text: The comparison is local for separated finite-type etale changes in each target and for open restrictions of each source. Indeed [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], with $f$ an identity, identifies the ordinary etale exceptional adjoint of an etale $u$ with $u^*$. For general $f$ it identifies $u^*f^\times$ with $(fu)^\times$ on source restrictions. Apply this to the etale arrows of a cartesian square and use the composition conjugation of Step 2 to get $u'^*f^!\cong f'^!u^*$. The finite exceptional inverse image is the ordinary etale right adjoint transported by comparison [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]; [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] identifies the bounded constructible domains, so the same identifications hold on the pro-etale category used here. Their compatibility with $\alpha$ follows by transposing: both paths are $\mathrm{Ku}_!$ followed by the pulled-back counits, by Step 2 and [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. By [lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative](1), isomorphy can therefore be checked after a target etale covering (and its pullback covering of the source), or after a source open covering. The schemes in this argument are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], and their separated finite-type maps admit the compactifications required in the ordinary etale statement, by [thm-nagata-compactification].

source.place: paragraphs 2 and 3: affine locality and etale-local reduction

proof.text:
For smooth maps of pure relative dimensions $d_1,d_2$, [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity] gives $f_i^!L_i\cong f_i^*L_i(d_i)[2d_i]$. More explicitly, first take a smooth map in one factor and the identity in the other. The purity comparison for its product with the identity sends
$$
f_1^*L_1(d_1)[2d_1]\boxtimes L_2
 \cong (f_1\times\operatorname{id})^!(L_1\boxtimes L_2).
$$
Monoidality of pullback is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]; the tensor formula and its arbitrary base-change compatibility are [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness](1),(3). This comparison is the $\alpha$ under consideration: the smooth purity map is adjoint to the projection formula followed by the smooth trace, so its transpose is the product compact-support map followed by the smooth counit and the identity counit. [thm-pur-smooth-base-change-coherence] identifies the purity map after taking the product with the identity. Doing the other factor and applying Step 2, [thm-pur-composition-coherence] identifies the composite with the purity comparison with total twist $d_1+d_2$ and shift $2d_1+2d_2$. Thus $\alpha$ is invertible in this case. The argument also supplies the identity-factor comparison with arbitrary finite-Tor coefficients, which will be needed in the factorization calculation; only its constant-coefficient consequence is used as the next reduction. The cited finite-coefficient smooth purity is the diagonal/DNC result, not an ambient exceptional-adjoint hypothesis. Smoothness and the relative dimensions of the identity-factor product maps are preserved by base change by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](1); composing them adds those dimensions by (2).

source.place: paragraph 2: smooth maps and normalization by the smooth trace

proof.text:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ be closed with open complement $j:V\hookrightarrow Y$, and let $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$, $Q\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$. Put $I=i\times\operatorname{id}_T$, $J=j\times\operatorname{id}_T$, $K=L\boxtimes Q$. The external-tensor image of the supported triangle and the supported triangle for $K$ are compared by [lem-sf-supported-external-triangle-comparison]. That lemma identifies the three components, including the connecting square, as $I_*\alpha_{i,\operatorname{id}}$ after the ordinary product identification, $1_K$, and the ordinary open product comparison.

The last component is invertible by [lem-trf-ordinary-kunneth]. Hence [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes the first component invertible. The first ordinary product identification is also invertible, so $I_*\alpha_{i,\operatorname{id}}$ is invertible. By [prop-sf-closed-unit-all-stages], $I_*$ is fully faithful: lift the inverse and use faithfulness on the two composite identities to see that $\alpha_{i,\operatorname{id}}$ is invertible. Factor interchange and the composition identity of Step 2 give a pair of closed immersions. The schemes $I,J$ are closed and open, respectively, by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]; they are complementary since their images are inverse images of $Z,V$. No regularity of $i$ is used.

source.place: paragraph 2: closed immersions, supported localization and ordinary open-product base change

proof.text: Now take $L_i=A_{Y_i}$. Choose affine opens $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i\subset Y_i$ and $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}C_i\subset f_i^{-1}(V_i)$ covering the sources. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], $C_i$ is a finitely generated $R_i$-algebra. Choosing generators gives a surjection $R_i[t_1,\ldots,t_{r_i}]\to C_i$, so by the affine characterization in [def-weil-closed-immersion] the restriction factors as $U_i\xrightarrow{h_i}\mathbf A^{r_i}_{V_i}\xrightarrow{p_i}V_i$, with $h_i$ closed. The projections are smooth of pure relative dimension $r_i$ by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]. Steps 5 and 6 apply to $p_1,p_2$ and to $h_1,h_2$, respectively; in the latter comparison use coefficients $p_i^!A_{V_i}$, which are in $D^b_{ctf}$ by [thm-sf-ctf-stability]. The composition identity of Step 2 identifies their invertible composite with $\alpha_{p_1h_1,p_2h_2}(A_{V_1},A_{V_2})$. Step 4 identifies this with the restriction of the original $\alpha$ to $U_1\times U_2$; those opens cover $X_1\times X_2$, so local detection gives the constant case globally. Finite direct sums give the case of finite free constant coefficients in both variables.

source.place: paragraph 2: affine closed/smooth factorization and finite free constants

proof.text: Suppose the $L_i$ are lisse sheaves with finite flat stalks. Their etale models exist by [lem-sf-proetale-locally-constant-origin]. Apply [fin2-lem-lisse-trivialized-finite-etale] to obtain finite etale surjective covers $P_i\to Y_i$ on whose connected components the sheaves are constant. Refine by these components and work on one component in each factor, with finite flat $A$-module fibers $M_i$. These are open components: $P_i$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]; it has finitely many irreducible components, and each connected component and its complement are finite unions of those closed subsets. Thus the refinement is an etale covering by separated finite-type schemes, as required in Step 4. Each $M_i$ is finitely presented: choose a finite generating set and a surjection $A^{r_i}\to M_i$; its kernel is a finite set because $A$ is finite, hence finitely generated. [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-flat-module-projective] makes $M_i$ projective. By the lifting characterization of [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], that surjection has a section, so $M_i$ is a retract of finite free $A^{r_i}$. The natural comparison on $(M_1,M_2)$ is consequently a retract of the comparison on $(A^{r_1},A^{r_2})$; naturality carries the section/retraction identities to source and target, and the corresponding section, inverse and retraction give its inverse. The latter comparison is invertible by Step 7. The products of the covers and their source pullbacks are covering families, so Step 4 descends invertibility. This is a local trivialization argument only; it does not assert that constants thickly generate global lisse sheaves.

source.place: paragraph 3: lisse coefficients and finite etale trivialization

proof.text:
Fix either coefficient variable. Pullback is exact by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], tensor is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], and compact support is exact by [lem-compact-support-direct-image-triangulated]. The canonical shift of its right adjoint is [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique]; [lem-sf-triangulated-right-adjoint] makes $f^!$ exact. All restrictions stay in $D^b_{ctf}$ by [thm-sf-ctf-stability]. Thus both sides of $\alpha$ are exact in either variable.

The geometric exchange and projection factors of Step 1 commute with shifts in either input by [lem-sf-finite-exchange-projection-commshift]. Compact-support composition and the specified exceptional counits commute with their canonical shifts by [lem-trf-finite-structural-maps-commshift](3),(4). Pullback monoidality and tensor shifts are those of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Composing and whiskering preserves these equations by [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker]; inverse isomorphisms preserve them by cancellation. Hence $\mathrm{Ku}_!$ followed by the counits commutes with shifts. The adjunction shift compatibility just cited carries this equation to its exceptional transpose $\alpha$. This checks the actual map, including its tensor signs. Now [lem-sf-triangle-two-out-of-three] applies in either variable and [lem-sf-generating-class-determination] makes its isomorphism locus thick. Exactness also gives the zero case.

source.place: paragraph 4: exactness, shift compatibility and thick propagation

proof.text:
Let $g_1:Z_1\to Y_1$ be either closed or open, with pullback $g_1':X_1'\to X_1$ and $f_1':X_1'\to Z_1$. Put $f=f_1\times f_2$, $F=f_1'\times f_2$, $G=g_1\times\operatorname{id}_{Y_2}$ and $G'=g_1'\times\operatorname{id}_{X_2}$. Step 3 and [lem-trf-ordinary-kunneth] identify the source and target of $\alpha_f(Rg_{1*}M_1,L_2)$ with
$$RG'_*(f_1'^!M_1\boxtimes f_2^!L_2),\qquad RG'_*F^!(M_1\boxtimes L_2),$$
respectively. These are precisely $\sigma,\tau$ in [lem-sf-exceptional-product-direct-image-compatibility]. Its equality identifies the specified comparison with $RG'_*\alpha_{f_1',f_2}(M_1,L_2)$, rather than just identifying its endpoints.

The second-variable clause of that lemma gives the same result after factor interchange with signed symmetry. Apply the first- and second-variable equalities successively for two direct images. A functor preserves an inverse, so invertibility on the changed targets implies invertibility on their direct images. All base-changed morphisms are separated finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]; the pullbacks of closed and open immersions remain so by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. The open case uses ordinary $R(-)_*$ throughout.

source.place: paragraph 5 and paragraph 6 opening: closed and open direct-image compatibility of alpha

proof.text:
Set up induction uniformly for all pairs of morphisms into nonempty separated finite-type $k$-schemes $Y_1,Y_2$, with $\dim Y_1+\dim Y_2\le D$, rather than treating a possibly nonclosed cohomological support as a closed subscheme. For example, for $j:\mathbf G_m\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1$, the nonvanishing locus of $j_!A$ is the nonclosed open $\mathbf G_m$. The blueprint's phrase $Z_i=\operatorname{supp}L_i$ must therefore mean closed support if it is to define a closed immersion; the generator closures below remove this ambiguity while retaining the same induction/localization route. Dimensions are finite by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]; empty target schemes have only zero coefficients and are already settled. Assume the assertion established for every smaller total dimension; for $D=0$ Steps 12--14 have empty boundary and use only the zero case.

By [lem-trf-devissage-generation] and the thick propagation of Step 9, it is enough to prove the assertion for pairs $L_i=Rg_{i*}j_{i!}F_i$, where $g_i:Z_i=\overline{U_i}\hookrightarrow Y_i$, $j_i:U_i\hookrightarrow Z_i$ is dense open and $F_i$ is lisse with flat finite stalks. Here taking the closure is part of the generator statement, not the assertion that the support of every constructible complex is closed. The dimension of a closed subspace is at most that of its ambient space, directly by viewing any chain of irreducible closed subsets as a chain in the ambient space. Step 10 therefore reduces this generator pair to the morphisms with targets $Z_i$, whose total dimension is still at most $D$, and coefficients $j_{i!}F_i$. Empty $Z_i$ give zero generators. This reduction does not invoke the induction hypothesis when the dimension stays equal to $D$; those pairs are proved in Steps 12--14.

source.place: paragraphs 4 and 5: the induction and closed-pushforward reduction to dense open strata

proof.text:
Rename the nonempty $Z_i$ of Step 11 as $Y_i$. Put $j=j_1\times j_2$, and let $j':X_1'\times X_2'\hookrightarrow X_1\times X_2$ and $f'=f_1'\times f_2'$ be its pullback and the restricted product morphism. Applying [lem-trf-ordinary-kunneth] twice, with the symmetry of external tensor, and using [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition], gives
$$
Rj_{1*}F_1\boxtimes Rj_{2*}F_2\cong Rj_*(F_1\boxtimes F_2).
$$
Explicitly the two target identifications are first the ordinary product map for $j_1$ with auxiliary $Rj_{2*}F_2$, then direct image by $j_1\times\operatorname{id}_{Y_2}$ of the ordinary product map for $j_2$ with auxiliary $F_1$ (after factor interchange). The resulting two direct images compose to $Rj_*$ because $(j_1\times\operatorname{id}_{Y_2})(\operatorname{id}_{U_1}\times j_2)=j$. On the source, first use the ordinary product map for $j_1'$ with auxiliary $Rj'_{2*}f_2'^!F_2$, then direct image by $j_1'\times\operatorname{id}_{X_2}$ of the product map for $j_2'$ with auxiliary $f_1'^!F_1$. Their composite direct image is $Rj'_*$, yielding
$$
Rj'_{1*}f_1'^!F_1\boxtimes Rj'_{2*}f_2'^!F_2
 \cong Rj'_*(f_1'^!F_1\boxtimes f_2'^!F_2).
$$
All auxiliary inputs, including $Rj_{i*}F_i$ and $f_i'^!F_i$, are in $D^b_{ctf}$ by [thm-sf-ctf-stability]. Step 3 supplies $f^!Rj_*\cong Rj'_*f'^!$ and its identity-factor versions. The open-map compatibility proved in Step 10 identifies $\alpha_f(Rj_{1*}F_1,Rj_{2*}F_2)$ with $Rj'_*\alpha_{f'}(F_1,F_2)$. The latter is invertible by the lisse case, Step 8, hence so is the former. This uses $Rj_*$ throughout; it makes no claim that $f^!$ commutes with $j_!$. The restricted morphisms are separated finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], and the pulled-back opens are open immersions by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change].

source.place: paragraph 6: passing through the two open direct images

proof.text:
For $C_i=Rj_{i*}F_i$, the open--closed triangle [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages] is
$$
B_i=j_{i!}F_i\longrightarrow C_i\longrightarrow
T_i=Ri_{i*}i_i^*C_i\longrightarrow B_i[1],
$$
where $i_i:W_i=Y_i\setminus U_i\hookrightarrow Y_i$. The identification $j_i^*Rj_{i*}F_i\cong F_i$ is the first assertion of [lem-exc-open-fully-faithful]. By [thm-sf-ctf-stability] all $C_i$, $i_i^*C_i$ and $T_i$ lie in $D^b_{ctf}$. Each $Y_i$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Because $U_i$ is dense open, $W_i$ is nowhere dense closed, so [lem-sc-hilbert-nowhere-dense-dimension-drop] gives $\dim W_i<\dim Y_i$ whenever $W_i$ is nonempty. If it is empty then $T_i=0$.

The induction hypothesis on the closed target pairs $(W_1,Y_2)$ and $(Y_1,W_2)$ applies to the coefficients $(i_1^*C_1,B_2)$ and $(C_1,i_2^*C_2)$, respectively. Each total target dimension is strictly smaller than the present one, and all four coefficients have the required finite-Tor constructible typing. The identity of Step 10 identifies the comparisons for $(T_1,B_2)$ and $(C_1,T_2)$ with the direct images of those two invertible comparisons under the corresponding base-changed closed product immersions. Direct image preserves their inverses, giving both required pairs on $(Y_1,Y_2)$. In dimension zero the nonempty boundaries would contradict the strict dimension drop, so both boundary terms are zero; this supplies the base case without assigning a dimension to an empty scheme.

source.place: paragraph 6: boundary triangles, finite-Tor typing and strict dimension drop

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-triangle-two-out-of-three] first in the second variable to $B_2\to C_2\to T_2\to B_2[1]$, with first variable $C_1$. Step 12 treats $(C_1,C_2)$ and Step 13 treats $(C_1,T_2)$, so it gives invertibility on $(C_1,B_2)$. Apply it next in the first variable to $B_1\to C_1\to T_1\to B_1[1]$, with second variable $B_2$. The pair just proved and $(T_1,B_2)$ from Step 13 give $(B_1,B_2)$. This finishes the generator pairs of Step 11 at dimension $D$. Apply [lem-sf-generating-class-determination] first in the second variable with each first-variable generator fixed, then in the first variable with each now arbitrary second variable fixed. Together with [lem-trf-devissage-generation] this proves every pair of coefficients at dimension $D$, completing the induction. Naturality holds throughout because the original map was defined as the transpose of the natural $\mathrm{Ku}_!$ and counits in [def-sf-kv-maps]; the inverse of a natural transformation with invertible components is natural by composing its naturality square with the two component inverses. Thus the specified $\alpha$ is an isomorphism natural in $L_1,L_2$.

source.place: paragraph 6 conclusion: two triangle arguments and completion of devissage
